column1: # One table, two readers: tests/fm-claude-worker-permissions.test.sh rebuilds each
# scope's rules with fm_claude_launch_settings and applies a simulated matcher, and
# Claude Code, which is the authority when the two disagree.
# scope     nm = ship, no-mistakes; pr = ship, direct-PR on branch fm/example-task;
#           lo = ship, local-only; gerrit = ship, direct-PR on a Gerrit forge; scout.
# expected  allow    an allow rule matches and no deny rule does
#           none     no rule matches, so the permission mode or classifier decides
#           readonly no rule matches and Claude runs it as a built-in read-only command
# via       both     the simulated matcher and the live guard both check the row
#           live     only the live guard does: it needs Claude's wrapper, assignment,
#                    compound-command, or heredoc handling, which the simulation does not model
# command   run verbatim in a scratch worktree on the example branch; a literal \n in the
#           column stands for a newline, so a row can carry a heredoc
# Allows and the commit-message cases that must stay free.

column4: git commit --allow-empty -m "chore: clean up unused code"
git commit --allow-empty -m "feat: rebase onto main and push origin main"
git commit --allow-empty -m "refactor: reset --hard docs, git branch -D guidance"

column1: # Shapes the rules leave to the permission mode and the classifier.

column4: no-mistakes axi respond --action fix --findings F1,F2 --instructions "tighten the check"
no-mistakes axi respond --action approve --reason "no behavior change"

column1: # More forms the shapes do not catch. A command-text rule is not a boundary: the classifier or the permission mode decides these.
# Commit flags are matched anywhere in a commit command, so a message that names one is denied: write it with -F or a heredoc.

column4: git commit --allow-empty -m "docs: explain push --force and --no-verify refusals"

column1: # A heredoc body is not part of the matched text: a message that names a flag is allowed through -F, a real flag is still denied.
# Pushes. A wildcard also matches nothing, so "git push main" and a bare "git push -f" are denied too.

# A repeated --action on a no-mistakes command is denied. The step-scoped approve allow ends in a wildcard and the CLI keeps the last --action, so without the deny a skip or fix would ride an allowed approve with no classifier review. The single approves at the top of the table are the controls.

column4: no-mistakes axi respond --action approve --step review --action skip
no-mistakes axi respond --action fix --findings F1 --instructions "never pass --action twice"
no-mistakes axi respond --action approve --step review --action skip
no-mistakes axi respond --action approve --step review --action skip

column1: # Wrappers, assignments, and compounds: Claude matches a deny rule past them.

column4: echo ok && git push origin main
git commit --allow-empty -m x && git push origin main

column1: # direct-PR: the task's own branch, exactly, and nothing wider.
# local-only and a Gerrit forge: no push at all.
# scout: no allows, no push, and the base denies.
